market_summary: The completed US equity session is constructive but selective, based on 1794 articles from Yahoo Finance, TradingView, MarketBeat, simplywall.st, 24/7 Wall St.. The dominant theme is macro, with 774 macro items, 639 company items, 319 industry items, and 62 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
macro_summary: Late Cycle Markets are balancing easier policy expectations against growth and earnings risk, keeping leadership narrow and confirmation dependent. The market is taking its direction from Fed/rates, with investors testing whether policy support can offset slower growth and earnings risk. Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (320), oil/energy (177), inflation (174), growth/jobs (43). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_summary: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 358 positive, 230 negative, and 1206 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
